title: EviDial: When Correct Depression Predictions Lack Evidence
abstract: arXiv:2610.27541v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Depression dialogue benchmarks commonly assess models by comparing predicted symptom labels with clinical scale scores. However, a prediction may agree with a benchmark label even when the dialogue lacks enough evidence to justify it. We introduce EviDial, a benchmark that distinguishes label agreement from evidence-grounded assessment. EviDial comprises 382 depression dialogues from three sources and 2,744 participant-symptom cells, each classified as having absent, partial, conflicting, or sufficient evidence. Because evidence sufficiency lacks a directly observable gold standard, we derive calibrated evidence references from multiple judgments using generalizability theory, many-facet Rasch measurement, and random-effects latent class analysis. translated_title: EviDial：当正确的抑郁预测缺乏证据时
translated_abstract: 抑郁对话基准通常通过将预测的症状标签与临床量表得分进行比较来评估模型。然而，即使对话中缺乏足够的证据来支持某个预测，该预测仍可能与基准标签一致。我们提出了EviDial，这是一个区分标签一致性与基于证据评估的基准。EviDial包含来自三个来源的382个抑郁对话和2,744个参与者-症状单元，每个单元被分类为无证据、部分证据、冲突证据或充分证据。由于证据充分性缺乏直接可观察的黄金标准，我们使用概化理论、多侧面Rasch测量和随机效应潜在类别分析，从多个判断中推导出经过校准的证据参考。我们的审计显示，82.8%的参与者-症状单元缺乏支持相应症状评估的充分文本证据，且各来源之间存在显著差异。
tldr: EviDial基准将“预测标签正确”与“有证据支撑的预测”区分开来，揭示82.8%的抑郁对话症状评估缺乏足够的文本证据支持。
en_tdlr: EviDial distinguishes label agreement from evidence-grounded assessment in depression prediction, revealing that 82.8% of dialogue-based symptom assessments lack sufficient textual evidence.
